title: Where Is Sass Used? knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which mental model best explains “Where Is Sass Used?” in Dart Sass?
options: Sass extends CSS with a compile-time layer for reusable values, expressions, rules, and module organization. The compiler transforms the source file into ordinary CSS; the browser does not execute Sass syntax.
The browser executes Sass source directly, so a compilation step is unnecessary.
Readable SCSS guarantees correct browser rendering, accessibility, and performance without output review.
The best solution is always to replace native CSS behavior with a new Sass abstraction.
questions.answer_key: Sass extends CSS with a compile-time layer for reusable values, expressions, rules, and module organization. The compiler transforms the source file into ordinary CSS; the browser does not execute Sass syntax.
questions.explanation: Sass extends CSS with a compile-time layer for reusable values, expressions, rules, and module organization. The compiler transforms the source file into ordinary CSS; the browser does not execute Sass syntax. The alternative choices confuse Sass compilation with browser execution or claim guarantees that require independent tests.

questions.prompt: When applying “Multi-page websites”, which approach is the most reliable?
options: Skip compilation and infer the final selector list and property values from the source file alone.
Prefer deeply nested selectors because fewer source lines always mean simpler and safer CSS.
Silence every warning before determining whether it identifies a deprecated or incorrect construct.
For multi-page websites, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.answer_key: For multi-page websites, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation.
questions.explanation: For multi-page websites, identify the relevant source rule, predict the intended result, and check the emitted CSS against that expectation. Compare the compiled output with the stated intent and preserve browser-native behavior where it is required.

Expose internal implementation details as public API and postpone documentation until after release.
